title: Adding Keys
goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to add a brand new key to a dictionary.
learn: Add a key with dict["new"] = value
Add more than one new key
idea: Dictionaries can grow. To add a new fact, assign to a key that is not there yet, like scores["Mia"] = 85. Python creates that key and stores the value for you.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change Mia's score to 99 and press Run. Mia should show 99 in the second print.

practice.text: Start with one player. Add Riley with score 70. Print the board.
practice.hint: Assign to a new key with square brackets, like board["Riley"] = 70. That adds Riley without changing Sam.
practice.starterTip: On the blank line, write board["Riley"] = 70, then run. Print(board) should show Sam and Riley.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if Riley: 70 is added and board is printed with both players.

practice.text: Add a "gems" key set to 3 on the bag, then print bag.
practice.hint: Assign to a key that is not there yet, like bag["gems"] = 3, and do it before print(bag).
practice.starterTip: Add bag["gems"] = 3 on the empty line. When you print, you should see coins and gems.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if gems key is added with value 3 and bag is printed.

quiz.question: How do you add a new key named Mia with value 85?
quiz.correct: Right, you assign to a new key with square brackets.
quiz.wrong: Use scores["Mia"] = 85 to add a key.

quiz.question: If the key is new, what does assignment do?
quiz.correct: Yes, a new key gets created and stored.
quiz.wrong: New keys get added when you assign to them.

quiz.question: After bag["potion"] = 2, can you look up bag["potion"]?
quiz.correct: Right, once a key is added you look it up like any other key.
quiz.wrong: New keys work the same way for lookup.
